source_quote: I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism the way you check anything borrowed before a fight: pull the string, sight down it, make sure the person who owned it before you wasn't sloppy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin closed on Jorlan after the glyph detonated, landing a critical Dawnbringer strike for 14 damage.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan. The explosion was still ringing through the cavern when Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted Zalthir could teleport to Ilvara or move her somewhere unpleasant.
source_quote: Zalthir said he could teleport directly to Ilvara — or grab her and move her somewhere unpleasant. I stored that.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the Glyph of Warding's trigger: any hostile creature crossing.
source_quote: The trigger: any hostile creature crossing. Invisible once finished.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observed Asha would hold the perimeter and not enter the fight at the start.
source_quote: She would not come in at the start. Once we initiated, she would hold the perimeter — anything coming from outside, she handles it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observed Jorlan as a threat with a location.
source_quote: Jorlan is not complicated. Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat because it tells you exactly where to aim.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin used the Sap to shove Jorlan off-balance, leaving him on the back foot with disadvantage.
source_quote: I pressed the Sap after it, using the momentum wrong to do something right — shoving him off-balance, leaving him on the back foot, disadvantage waiting for him the next time he tried to hit back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin watched Grygum inscribe the Glyph of Warding into the bridge stone.
source_quote: Grygum took the bridge. Jorlan's side. He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself...

subject: thorin's sap maneuver
fact: After the glyph detonated, Thorin pressed the attack with Dawnbringer, landing a critical hit for 14 damage and using Sap to shove Jorlan off-balance.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan... Dawnbringer came down — crit... 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to... I pressed the Sap after it...

subject: Thorin's tactical observation
fact: Thorin noted that Jorlan was a threat with a location — predictable and targetable.
source_quote: Jorlan is not complicated. Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat because it tells you exactly where to aim.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir disengaged and went straight up ten feet, hovering in that particular way of someone who has made the tactically correct decision and is not happy about it.
source_quote: He disengaged and went straight up. Ten feet. Clear of the worst of the cloud, hovering in that particular way of someone who has made the tactically correct decision and is not happy about it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir landed two strikes on Ilvara totaling thirty-one damage.
source_quote: The second strike came with her pinned and her options narrowed. Advantage. Fifteen more. Thirty-one total.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted Ilvara's scream was left behind on purpose.
source_quote: The scream still echoed off the cave walls like she'd left it there on purpose.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Ilvara screamed at herself, not at him.
source_quote: She screamed. Not at me. The GM's exact words: *at herself.* And I caught that...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed Ilvara dissolved into fungal matter and reappeared elsewhere.
source_quote: She came apart into the fungal matter beneath her feet — flowed through it like water pouring into a crack...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir registered the toxin as a subtle wrongness in how he moved, a falter in the stride of someone who had been pressing a meaningful advantage over Ilvara.
source_quote: I watched the dragonborn's body register the toxin — not a dramatic collapse, nothing so clean as that — just a subtle wrongness in how he moved, a falter in the stride of someone who had been, until thirty seconds ago, pressing a meaningful advantage over Ilvara.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said he was out of actions and bonus actions, and would just kind of look on and be confused.
source_quote: "I'm out of actions and bonus actions," he said, from somewhere above the spore line, "so I guess I'll just kind of look on and be confused."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir teleported to Ilvara and grabbed her before she could react.
source_quote: I stepped through the dark and arrived before she'd finished deciding what to do...

subject: zalthir's reflection on valen
fact: Zalthir silently reflected on Valen — who had once been exactly what the servants were — and noted the loss of identity between then and now.
source_quote: Then he reflected on Valen. Not out loud, really — it was more in the quality of the silence that followed. I felt the thought land in the room anyway. Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.

subject: Zalthir's tactical exhaustion
fact: Zalthir was out of actions and bonus actions after teleporting and grappling Ilvara, leaving him with altitude and view but no further capacity.
source_quote: I hung in the air. Out of actions. Out of bonus actions. Out of everything I'd had when I arrived...

subject: Zalthir's teleport
fact: Zalthir teleported directly to Ilvara or grabbed her and moved her somewhere unpleasant.
source_quote: Zalthir said he could teleport directly to Ilvara — or grab her and move her somewhere unpleasant.

subject: Zalthir's Teleport and Grapple
fact: Zalthir teleported directly onto Ilvara’s platform, grappled her, and delivered two devastating strikes totaling 31 damage. He attempted to drag her into the Dust of Suleiman zone, but she dissolved into fungal matter and reappeared elsewhere, escaping his grasp. The event revealed Ilvara’s ability to merge with the fungus and her psychological unraveling — she screamed at herself, not at Zalthir.
source_quote: I drove the weapon in. Sixteen... The second strike came with her pinned... Thirty-one total... She screamed... at herself... Between one heartbeat and the next, she came apart into the fungal matter beneath her feet... My hands closed on nothing.

subject: Zalthir's teleport strike
fact: Zalthir teleported into combat range without warning, catching the target mid-decision and delivering a lethal strike — demonstrating mastery of surprise and timing.
source_quote: I drove the weapon in. Sixteen. The grip locked.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a figure whose magical items are offered as payment, but are suspected of contamination — suggesting she is either compromised or dangerous.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara's cult is a splinter group that worships a corrupted interpretation of Lolth as a bride; its members have been transformed into mindless fungal entities, suggesting a pervasive and infectious magical corruption tied to Zuggtmoy or similar fungal deities.
source_quote: all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Lolth
fact: Lolth is invoked as the source of spiritual compensation, with Asha Vandree claiming her gratitude is already received — a claim that signals detachment from conventional worship.
source_quote: The gratitude of Lolth. I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that.

subject: the Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is the organization to which the sculpting mage belongs, known for precision destructive magic.
source_quote: I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.

subject: The Fungal Cult of Ilvara
fact: The Fungal Cult of Ilvara is a splinter group that worships the Big Heart Fungus as a divine manifestation of Lolth’s will. It spreads through spores, transforms followers into mindless fungal entities, and operates in close proximity to corrupted sites. Its members are not willingly loyal but biologically compromised. The cult is the primary adversary in this operation.
source_quote: All of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve is a former drow military organization whose guards have been repurposed into fungal weapons by Ilvara and Zuggtmoy’s influence. Once soldiers with names, duties, and agency, they are now mindless tools directed by the cavern’s fungal will. Their transformation represents the collapse of institutional identity under supernatural corruption. Their existence is a grim monument to what happens when loyalty is overwritten by biological domination.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed

subject: Velkynvelve Guards
fact: Former guards of Velkynvelve, now repurposed as mindless weapons by Ilvara’s fungal corruption under Zuggtmoy’s influence; they are no longer choosing to move but are directed, their identities erased by colonization.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed...

subject: Zuggtmoy cult
fact: The Zuggtmoy cult is represented by the icon on the battlefield — its presence signals active corruption, and its survival would allow the seed of its influence to spread.
source_quote: A Zuggtmoy-aligned symbol of office left standing is not a symbol — it's a seed.

subject: Zuggtmoy’s Influence
fact: Zuggtmoy’s influence is the ancient, fungal corruption that underlies the transformation of the Velkynvelve guards and the Heart Fungus’s dominance. It is not a direct actor, but a pervasive force that repurposes life into tools of decay. Its presence is felt in the way bodies dissolve into matter, how minds are erased, and how the battlefield remembers death. Ilvara is its conduit — not its master. The faction is not a group, but a parasitic principle of existence that consumes will and rewrites flesh.
source_quote: fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible through Ilvara's particular corruption

subject: Big Heart Fungus cloud
fact: The Big Heart Fungus detonated a twenty-foot cloud of spore-thick poison that hung in the air like a settled entity.
source_quote: The cloud didn't drift... This hung in the cavern air like it had decided to stay — twenty feet of spore-thick poison...

subject: bridge
fact: The bridge contains a Glyph of Warding, placed with exactly this kind of chaos in mind.
source_quote: We'd placed it with exactly this kind of chaos in mind

subject: Bridge
fact: The bridge is the site of the Glyph of Warding and Jorlan’s fatal charge; it is a chokepoint where tactical misjudgment leads to catastrophic consequences.
source_quote: We'd laid it on the bridge like a welcome mat...

subject: bridge
fact: The bridge is the site where Jorlan ran toward the Glyph, convinced he was reaching his prize.
source_quote: he came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome. ... when you're already running at what you think is your prize.

subject: bridge
fact: The bridge is the site where the Glyph of Warding detonated, causing force and light to erupt in a sphere.
source_quote: The Glyph fired. Force and light erupted outward in a sphere, the kind of detonation that doesn't care who's in the way.

subject: bridge
fact: The bridge was the chosen site for the glyph trap — a narrow, defensible chokepoint where Jorlan’s advance was inevitable and his evasion impossible.
source_quote: He came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome.

subject: Bridge
fact: The bridge was the site of the Glyph of Warding inscription and Jorlan's stationary position.
source_quote: Jorlan's side. He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself...

subject: bridge elevation
fact: The bridge bore the Glyph of Warding, placed with the expectation of chaotic combat, and was the focal point of Jorlan's fatal advance.
source_quote: The Glyph of Warding on the bridge was still live. We'd placed it with exactly this kind of chaos in mind...

subject: Bridge of the Glyph of Warding
fact: The Bridge of the Glyph of Warding is a narrow crossing over the cavern, inscribed with an invisible trap triggered by hostile movement. It is the only direct path to Ilvara’s platform and is guarded by Jorlan. Its placement defines the tactical axis of the battle, and its invisibility makes it a psychological weapon as much as a physical one.
source_quote: Jorlan... started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself... The bridge looked like a bridge again.

subject: Bridge with Glyph of Warding
fact: The bridge is a focal point of tactical design — a deliberately placed trap zone where the Glyph of Warding remains active. It was placed with chaotic battlefield conditions in mind, and its presence was known to the party. Jorlan’s movement toward it was predictable, and his approach triggered the trap. The bridge is not just a path — it is a lure, a weaponized geometry of the battlefield, and a symbol of how preparedness can be turned against the unobservant.
source_quote: The Glyph of Warding on the bridge was still live.

subject: cavern
fact: The cavern became a zone of cascading magical disruption after the glyph and fireball detonated — the environment itself was warped by overlapping effects.
source_quote: The cavern went briefly and magnificently wrong in all the right ways.

subject: cavern
fact: The cavern was ten minutes ago merely dangerous, but became a space filled with fire, spore, and disruption.
source_quote: a space that had, ten minutes ago, been merely dangerous — 'than I had any right to expect.'

subject: cavern
fact: The cavern went briefly and magnificently wrong in all the right ways after the overlapping spells.
source_quote: The cavern went briefly and magnificently wrong in all the right ways.

subject: Cavern Floor
fact: The cavern floor became a battleground where fungal matter flowed, Dust of Suleiman lay in wait, and Ilvara reappeared after dissolving into spores.
source_quote: She came apart into the fungal matter beneath her feet — flowed through it like water pouring into a crack, like smoke running back into the dark — and reappeared somewhere else on the cavern floor.

subject: Cavern Floor
fact: The cavern floor is not passive terrain but an active conduit of Zuggtmoy’s corruption, capable of raising and directing the spore servants; its fungal network is the hidden engine of the enemy’s power.
source_quote: Rising from the cavern floor with the patient, purposeless movement of things that are no longer choosing to move...

subject: cavern floor
fact: The cavern floor is the origin of the spore servants, repurposed by Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: Rising from the cavern floor with the patient, purposeless movement of things that are no longer choosing to move — they are simply directed.

subject: Cavern floor
fact: The cavern floor was the site of Ilvara's transformation, the Dust of Suleiman hazard, and the fungal cloud.
source_quote: She reappeared somewhere else on the cavern floor... I looked at the Dust of Suleiman area... twenty feet of spore-thick poison, sitting in the middle of the battlefield...

subject: Cavern Floor (Dust of Suleiman Area)
fact: The cavern floor, particularly the Dust of Suleiman area, is not inert terrain — it is a living substrate of fungal growth, reanimation, and decay. It absorbed Ilvara’s body, flowed through her, and expelled her elsewhere. It is the medium through which the Heart Fungus operates and where the Velkynvelve guards rose from. The floor is the battlefield’s true commander — the entity that remembers, repurposes, and retaliates. The party’s tactical calculations ignore it at their peril.
source_quote: the fungal matter beneath her feet — flowed through it like water pouring into a crack

subject: cavern floor elevation
fact: The cavern floor was the origin point of the spore servants and the fungal threat — the battlefield's anchor, once passive, now an active enemy.
source_quote: The fight was far from over. But the battlefield had shifted in our favor... the Big Heart Fungus. Still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield.

subject: Cavern of the Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Cavern of the Big Heart Fungus is a subterranean chamber where Ilvara resides, saturated with spores and dominated by the massive fungal organism. The air is thick with persistent poison, the floor is partially liquefied by fungal growth, and the space is saturated with unnatural stillness. It is a hostile environment where movement is dangerous, perception is distorted, and the fungus itself is an active participant in combat.
source_quote: The cloud didn't drift. That was the first thing I noticed. Normal smoke drifts. Normal gas disperses. This hung in the cavern air like it had decided to stay — twenty feet of spore-thick poison, sitting in the middle of the battlefield as if it belonged there.

subject: Dust of Suleiman zone
fact: The Dust of Suleiman area was a tactical hazard on the cavern floor, intended to turn the priestess into someone else's problem.
source_quote: I looked at the Dust of Suleiman area... priestess plus that zone equals someone else's problem.

subject: Elevated platform
fact: The elevated platform was the initial position of Ilvara, and the site of Zalthir's teleport and first strike.
source_quote: One moment I was reading the geometry of the space — the elevated platform... and the next I was already there, adjacent...

subject: Elevated Platform
fact: Zalthir arrived on the elevated platform, adjacent to Ilvara, inside the radius where a priestess stops being an authority and becomes a target.
source_quote: One moment I was reading the geometry of the space — the elevated platform, the sightlines, the gap between us and her — and the next I was already there, adjacent, inside the radius where a priestess stops being an authority and becomes a target.

subject: Elevated Platform (Ilvara's Position)
fact: The Elevated Platform is the raised dais where Ilvara stands, offering her sightlines and authority over the cavern. It is the primary objective of the assault. Zalthir’s teleportation brought him directly into this space, disrupting Ilvara’s command presence and triggering the confrontation. The platform is now a zone of intense tactical pressure.
source_quote: One moment I was reading the geometry of the space — the elevated platform, the sightlines, the gap between us and her — and the next I was already there, adjacent, inside the radius where a priestess stops being an authority and becomes a target.

subject: Far End of Battlefield
fact: The location of the Big Heart Fungus, which remains untouched and central to the conflict; it is the anchor point that defines the battlefield’s geometry and the party’s strategic imperative.
source_quote: Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield.

subject: Grygum's crossbow position
fact: Grygum had a light crossbow; Thorin borrowed it and checked its mechanism before the fight.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction... I checked the mechanism...

subject: Jorlan's position
fact: Jorlan was a threat with a location — stationary on the bridge, inscribing the Glyph of Warding.
source_quote: I looked at Jorlan across that bridge... Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat...

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is referenced by Daz as the environment where Ilvara survived through social cunning.
source_quote: she did not survive this long in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem by being slow

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is the source of the corrupting mushroom artifact — a place of unnatural growth, forbidden knowledge, and lethal enchantments.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Neverlight Grove artifact
fact: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: problem zone
fact: The area containing Zalthir and Thorin was the focus of protective sculpting, remaining untouched by the fireball.
source_quote: Zalthir and Thorin are inside the problem zone.

subject: Site of Negotiation
fact: The location where the narrator and Asha Vandree met is a place where illusions, oozes, and fungal corruption intersect; it is sufficiently remote and strange to allow for the concealment of Glabbagool and the plausibility of Ilvara’s influence.
source_quote: I came to you in my smaller form, and led you here.

subject: spore line
fact: The spore line is the boundary above which Zalthir hovers, separating him from the worst of the cloud.
source_quote: hovering in that particular way of someone who has made the tactically correct decision and is not happy about it. ... from somewhere above the spore line

subject: spore line elevation
fact: The spore line hung above the cavern floor, marking the boundary from which characters spoke while hovering — a tactical vantage point.
source_quote: from somewhere above the spore line

subject: The Bridge
fact: The bridge is a chokepoint where Jorlan has inscribed a Glyph of Warding — now a silent, deadly barrier controlling all movement across it.
source_quote: He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Twenty feet of maintained distance
fact: Twenty feet of maintained distance was the established safety buffer between infected and uninfected.
source_quote: Twenty feet of maintained distance. Separate food.

subject: Underdark equivalent of a table
fact: The party spread out tactical options on the Underdark equivalent of a table while crouched in the dark.
source_quote: Then the party spread out the options on the table, or whatever the Underdark equivalent of a table is when you're crouched in the dark...

subject: Underdark equivalent of a table
fact: The party spread out the options on the Underdark equivalent of a table when crouched in the dark with a drow informant and a borrowed crossbow.
source_quote: Then the party spread out the options on the table, or whatever the Underdark equivalent of a table is when you're crouched in the dark with a drow informant and a borrowed crossbow.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus detonated a twenty-foot spore-thick poison cloud that hung in the cavern air like it had decided to stay — as if it belonged there, as if it had always belonged there, as if we were the interlopers in its home.
source_quote: The cloud didn't drift. That was the first thing I noticed. Normal smoke drifts. Normal gas disperses. This hung in the cavern air like it had decided to stay — twenty feet of spore-thick poison, sitting in the middle of the battlefield as if it belonged there, as if it had always belonged there, as if we were the interlopers in its home.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus is a sentient, massive fungal organism that serves as the source of Ilvara’s corruption and the primary weapon of the Fungal Cult. It emits a persistent, non-dispersing spore cloud, infects creatures on contact, and regenerates slowly. It cannot be killed quickly or easily. It is not merely a hazard — it is an active, territorial entity that views intruders as invaders.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption. The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus is still standing, anchoring the far end of the battlefield, and remains the reason Zalthir is hovering.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus. Still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield. Still the reason Zalthir was hovering above the fight instead of in it.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The central anchor of the battlefield, still standing after multiple assaults; it is the root cause of the conflict, responsible for Zalthir’s aerial position and the need for decisive resource expenditure.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus. Still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dawnbringer blade
fact: The Dawnbringer blade delivered a critical strike to Jorlan after the glyph — its holy light cut cleanly, dealing 14 damage and exploiting his vulnerability from the earlier blast.
source_quote: Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Fungal Creatures
fact: Fungal Creatures are mindless, infected beings transformed by the Big Heart Fungus. They are former allies of Ilvara, now reduced to biological extensions of the fungus. They lack individuality, act on instinct, and serve as both guards and vectors of corruption. They are not enemies of choice but consequences of exposure.
source_quote: All of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Fungal Creatures
fact: Fungal creatures are mindless, transformed followers of Ilvara; they are the result of a magical corruption that turns sentient beings into inert, spore-based entities, likely tied to Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Fungal creatures
fact: Ilvara's allies had turned into mindless fungal creatures, a sign of her corruption.
source_quote: all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Fungalized Velkynvelve Guards
fact: Four former Velkynvelve guards rose from the cavern floor with patient, purposeless movement — no longer choosing to act, but being directed. Their bodies had been repurposed through fungal colonization under Zuggtmoy’s influence, corrupted further by Ilvara’s will. Once drow with names, duties, and opinions, they are now weapons pointed at the party. Zalthir recognized their tragedy, reflecting on Valen — one of them who could have become this. Their existence embodies the fragility of identity under conquest and corruption.
source_quote: Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot.

subject: Gelatinous Familiar
fact: A gelatinous familiar accompanies Asha Vandree — an unconventional companion suggesting her alignment with unnatural, fungal, or ooze-based entities.
source_quote: a gelatinous familiar was, on balance, the best available instrument for killing someone she needed dead.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock; his eyes drifted left and right with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before.
source_quote: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock. The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before and doesn't fully understand why it's being asked to start now.

subject: Glabbagool's eyes
fact: Glabbagool's eyes drifted left and right with unhurried curiosity, giving him away as not a rock.
source_quote: The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity...

subject: Grey Ooze (Glabbagool)
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient grey ooze functioning as a bound familiar to the narrator; his unnatural eye movements and inability to maintain geological disguise reveal his non-rock nature and lack of experience with deception.
source_quote: The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before and doesn't fully understand why it's being asked to start now.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a sentient, non-scenic organism that detonated a twenty-foot cloud of spore-thick poison across the cavern floor. It did not disperse like normal gas — it hung deliberately, as if claiming the space as its own. It was observed since the party’s entry, and its activation confirmed prior notes: it is not scenery. It is an active, hostile entity that shifted the battlefield’s dynamics, turning the floor itself into an enemy. Its spore cloud poisoned Zalthir and forced tactical retreats, proving it to be a primary combatant rather than environmental hazard.
source_quote: that's not a metaphor. I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: Ilvara's fungal transformation
fact: Ilvara transformed into fungal matter and reappeared elsewhere, indicating a connection to the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: She came apart into the fungal matter beneath her feet — flowed through it like water pouring into a crack... and reappeared somewhere else...

subject: spore servant
fact: The spore servant is a former Velkynvelve guard repurposed by Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed, the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible

subject: spore servant
fact: Twenty-one spore servants were caught in the glyph detonation — one was obliterated, others staggered and barely held together, their cohesion shattered by the blast.
source_quote: One servant came apart completely. Just gone. The others staggered; I watched one barely hold together, listing like a wall with one stone pulled from its base.

subject: spore servant count
fact: Four spore servants rose from the cavern floor with patient, purposeless movement — former Velkynvelve guards repurposed by Zuggtmoy's influence through Ilvara's corruption.
source_quote: Four shapes. Rising from the cavern floor with the patient, purposeless movement of things that are no longer choosing to move — they are simply directed. Former Velkynvelve guards.

subject: spore servant count
fact: One spore servant ceased to be a problem after the glyph detonated, while others staggered in a way suggesting they had not enjoyed the experience.
source_quote: One spore servant ceased to be a problem. The others staggered in a way that suggested they had not enjoyed the experience.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Fungal reanimated drow warriors, corrupted by Zuggtmoy’s influence and controlled by Ilvara; they stagger after the Glyph and Fireball, one destroyed outright, others barely holding together, demonstrating vulnerability to area effects.
source_quote: One servant came apart completely. Just gone.

subject: The Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus is the primary weapon of corruption — a persistent, non-lethal entity that resists quick destruction and requires sustained damage.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: the fireball
fact: The fireball behaved as directed — it did not consume Zalthir and Thorin, and struck only Ilvara and the icon, demonstrating non-sentient obedience to arcane intent.
source_quote: It will go around — not because fire cares, fire doesn't care about anything, but because I told it the shape of what it cannot touch.

subject: Zuggtmoy icon
fact: The Zuggtmoy icon, representing a living seed of corruption, was targeted by Daz’s Fireball and rendered unstable — its presence on the battlefield was no longer passive but actively dangerous.
source_quote: A Zuggtmoy-aligned symbol of office left standing is not a symbol — it's a seed. You don't leave seeds.

subject: Asha
fact: Asha is referenced by Daz as the source of the stakes that prevent him from filing away the mission's importance.
source_quote: Asha was explicit enough about what's riding on this that I haven't been able to fully file it away

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who has seen through deception and constructed a coherent belief system around delusion, accepting a spore-maddened wizard with followers and a gelatinous familiar as the best available instrument to kill Ilvara. She remains uninfected through devotion and maintains a 20-foot distance from corrupted allies. Her hatred for Ilvara is genuine, not tactical, and she offers magical items — possibly contaminated — as payment.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who survived long enough to find spore-maddened lunatics willing to close lethal distance for her, using devotion as her shield and hatred as her weapon.
source_quote: I was going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a drow who treats information as currency and deception as a professional skill; she has seen multiple iterations of the same con involving false divine possession by Lolth, and has chosen to accept the narrator as a deluded but potentially useful mage after rejecting his initial claim.
source_quote: Oh, dear goodness, have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? Convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced by Jorlan as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow, and whose hatred for Ilvara has been building in close quarters with a corrupted superior.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree offered Ilvara’s magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated, and filed that caveat.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated. I noted that caveat. I filed it.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Bahamut is referenced as possibly watching, though notes are taken either way.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching. I took notes either way.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes he is a deluded magic user with spores within him.
source_quote: Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz calculated the battlefield and chose to cast the Dust of Suleiman and a concentrated Fireball despite resource cost, targeting Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon simultaneously to maximize disruption.
source_quote: The priorities are clear: Ilvara, and the icon. In that order, or really in no particular order — they're the same problem wearing different faces.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz calculated the placement of Fireball to overlap Ilvara and the icon, using Sculpt Spells to avoid allies.
source_quote: Both targets, one sphere, and the geometry cooperates if I'm exact. ... I carve them out.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz executes a precisely sculpted Fireball at fourth level, simultaneously striking Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon while sparing Zalthir and Thorin; he calculates target priority with clinical precision and views tactical success as a matter of measurable change on the board.
source_quote: That worked better than I had any right to expect.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a wizard who attempted to pass as a divinely touched follower of Lolth but was exposed as a con artist. He pivoted to playing a deluded, spore-infected mage with genuine but misunderstood power, successfully convincing Asha Vandree that his madness is a viable asset. He retains the persona with steadiness, not eloquence, and has recruited followers and bound a gelatinous familiar, Glabbagool, as part of his performance.
source_quote: Perhaps my prayers have been answered through this… confused vessel… Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it. And by the way, I've convinced others to join me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced as having found purpose in precision and force, rejecting the notion that precision is the opposite of force.
source_quote: Precision is not the opposite of force. It is force, directed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by Grygum as the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by Grygum as the one who cast the Fireball that overlapped with the Dust of Suleiman.
source_quote: Then Daz's shaped Fireball hit — Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon both, simultaneously

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard, and finds purpose in reading the board and identifying highest-value targets.
source_quote: I have found purpose. I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Ilvara half-saved the Fireball, which was professionally irritating but not unexpected.
source_quote: She half-saves, which is professionally irritating but not unexpected

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Ilvara survived long in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem by not being slow.
source_quote: she did not survive this long in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem by being slow

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's damage to Ilvara and the icon was twelve each.
source_quote: Ilvara takes twelve. The icon takes twelve.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's geometry cooperated because he was exact.
source_quote: the geometry cooperates if I'm exact

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's outcome changed the math of the fight in their favor.
source_quote: Twelve points is twelve points and the board looks different than it did thirty seconds ago, and that is the only metric that has ever mattered.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's placement was the most useful thing he knows how to do.
source_quote: It is perhaps the most useful thing I know how to do.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's success was a bet on precision overriding the need for coverage.
source_quote: But coverage is not what I need. I need placement.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Fireball's success was not remarkable because it was the plan, and he noticed anyway.
source_quote: Plans working is not remarkable. But I notice.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the icon and Ilvara were still standing after the Fireball.
source_quote: The icon is still standing. Ilvara is still standing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the stakes were not abstract — they were Asha and everything she told him.
source_quote: The stakes are not abstract. The stakes are Asha, and everything she told me

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said nothing about Zalthir and Thorin being unsinged, though he noted it.
source_quote: I note that Zalthir is unsinged. I note that Thorin is unsinged. I don't say anything about it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous ooze familiar bound to Daz, whose attempts to pass as a rock during negotiations failed due to untrained eye movements. Asha Vandree accepts him as part of the deluded-mage archetype — strange, uncategorizable, and fitting the profile of a mage with unusual, nontraditional power. He is not a combatant but a living symbol of the madness Daz projects.
source_quote: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock. The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a grey ooze creature attempting to pass as a rock during negotiations; his eyes betray him with unhurried, unnatural movement, indicating he has never before been asked to pretend to be geological and lacks the instinct for such deception.
source_quote: The eyes gave him away. They drifted left. They drifted right. They did this with the unhurried curiosity of a creature that has never needed to pretend to be geological before and doesn't fully understand why it's being asked to start now.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum called Jorlan an idiot and invited him toward the Glyph, betting on ego overriding tactical awareness.
source_quote: You call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum called out, 'Come get it, idiot,' and detonated the Glyph of Warding.
source_quote: Grygum called out. 'Come get it, idiot.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum devised and triggered the glyph trap, baiting Jorlan with taunts and expressing genuine surprise when it succeeded — his tactical gamble on ego over awareness paid off.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot." && "I didn't expect it to work.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had a light crossbow, handed it over without drama, and was confirmed as not sloppy in maintenance.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism... He wasn't. That dwarf is okay.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had the idea for the Glyph of Warding, or at least voiced it.
source_quote: The Glyph was Grygum's idea, or at least Grygum's mouth.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a dwarf who carries a light crossbow, understands the danger of the Neverlight Grove artifact, and refuses to touch it — his silence with Thorin a blood oath.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum laid the Glyph of Warding on the bridge as a bait trap, anticipating ego-driven aggression; he calls out to Jorlan with deliberate provocation and expresses genuine surprise when the trap succeeds.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan came across the bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome.
source_quote: he came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan took the full force of the Glyph and now the Dawnbringer strike.
source_quote: He'd taken the full force of the Glyph and now this.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan was not having his best moment after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: Jorlan himself was not having his best moment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that Jorlan's certainty was almost giant-brained, and that giants are usually right about the terrain.
source_quote: There's something almost giant-brained about that kind of certainty. Giants move like that. ... The problem is, giants are usually right about the terrain.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Dust of Suleiman was committed because the creature had already demonstrated what it was willing to do.
source_quote: because the creature had already demonstrated what it was willing to do to us and I had no interest in finding out what it would do next if left unaddressed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Dust of Suleiman was not a small resource, and he made the decision anyway.
source_quote: This was not a small resource. I made the decision anyway

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph was placed by the group's execution, not just Grygum's idea.
source_quote: The placement was all of us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph was placed like a welcome mat.
source_quote: We'd laid it on the bridge like a welcome mat

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph worked because they stopped expecting it to work.
source_quote: you stop expecting it, almost. You get tactical, you do the work, you lay the trap in exactly the right place — and then somewhere between placing it and watching it detonate, you forget to believe in yourself.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph's detonation caused a sphere of force and light that didn't care who was in the way.
source_quote: Force and light erupted outward in a sphere, the kind of detonation that doesn't care who's in the way.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the Glyph's detonation caused twenty-one damage to the cluster.
source_quote: Twenty-one damage blooming through the cluster all at once

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the battlefield fragmented faster than any of them had planned for.
source_quote: The battlefield had fragmented faster than any of us had planned for, allies pulled in three different directions by pressure we hadn't fully mapped before we walked in.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the battlefield had shifted in their favor after the combined spells.
source_quote: The battlefield had shifted in our favor

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the difference between soldiers and weapons is sometimes just time and circumstance, and he filed that thought away under 'things not to dwell on mid-combat.'
source_quote: I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the difference between soldiers and weapons is sometimes just time and circumstance.
source_quote: Soldiers. Now weapons. The difference between the two is sometimes just time and circumstance

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the fight was far from over, even after the combined spells.
source_quote: The fungus was still standing. The fight was far from over.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the spore servant that barely held together was listing like a wall with one stone pulled from its base.
source_quote: I watched one barely hold together, listing like a wall with one stone pulled from its base.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the spore servant that came apart completely was just gone.
source_quote: One servant came apart completely. Just gone.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted that the spore servants staggered in a way that suggested they had not enjoyed the experience.
source_quote: The others staggered in a way that suggested they had not enjoyed the experience.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted the conditions that made the Glyph work: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.
source_quote: I noted the specific combination of factors that had produced that outcome: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed that the spell worked better than expected, and values honest tactical assessment.
source_quote: *"That worked better than I had any right to expect."*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'I didn't expect it to work,' after the Glyph detonated, with honesty.
source_quote: 'I didn't expect it to work.' That last part was honest.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'Kaboom,' and then, 'I didn't expect it to work,' with genuine surprise.
source_quote: Grygum said, 'Kaboom!' And then, with something like genuine surprise underneath it: 'I didn't expect it to work.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum said, 'That worked better than I had any right to expect,' after Daz's Fireball.
source_quote: Grygum's voice cuts through the settling heat: 'That worked better than I had any right to expect.'

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara absorbed the combined effects of the Fireball and glyph detonation, taking punishment she hadn't budgeted for — her position was compromised, and she was left vulnerable.
source_quote: Ilvara absorbing punishment she hadn't budgeted for

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a drow priestess of Ilvara who was grappled and constrained mid-combat, her movement fully controlled until she dissolved into fungal matter beneath her feet. She screamed at herself — a sign of her fury at having been hurt, and at the breaking of an illusion that her core self was inviolable. She is now out of reach, having put distance between herself and her attacker, and her scream lingers in the cavern as if left there deliberately.
source_quote: at herself.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become corrupted by the Big Heart Fungus, believing Lolth wishes to be married. Her influence has turned allies into mindless fungal creatures. She is the target of Asha Vandree’s vendetta and the central threat of the operation. Her corruption is not merely magical but spiritual, and her transformation is irreversible without destruction.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her… all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become seduced by the delusion that Lolth wishes to be married; her followers have been transformed into mindless fungal creatures, and her corruption is spreading, inspiring deep, personal hatred in Asha Vandree.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Daz as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Ilvara might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is the orchestrator of the fungal corruption, having raised four former Velkynvelve guards as directed weapons under Zuggtmoy’s influence; she is targeted by Daz’s Fireball and absorbs significant damage but remains standing.
source_quote: Then Ilvara called them up.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara took twelve points of damage from the fireball, surviving due to her proficiency in Menzoberranzan's social ecosystem.
source_quote: She takes twelve. The icon takes twelve.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara's corruption made visible the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence through the repurposed Velkynvelve guards.
source_quote: Former Velkynvelve guards. I recognized the posture of soldiers whose bodies had been repurposed, the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible through Ilvara's particular corruption.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan committed to advancing across the bridge despite the glyph trap, demonstrating total confidence that proved fatal — he took full force of the detonation and was left reeling, unable to evade the follow-up strike.
source_quote: He came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a combatant who, in the midst of chaotic battlefield conditions, was drawn toward the Glyph of Warding on the bridge. He was distracted and angry enough that he failed to track the floor’s danger. An opponent calculated his trajectory in one second and baited him into the trap with the call, 'Come get it, idiot.' His movement was a predictable response to pressure, and his action was a catalyst for the next phase of the battlefield’s retaliation.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a drow who charges recklessly into Grygum’s Glyph of Warding, trusting his own certainty over tactical awareness; he takes full damage from the explosion and is later struck by Thorin’s Dawnbringer, leaving him compromised and off-balance.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is an uninfected human who resists corruption through hatred, serves as a tactical anchor, and inscribes Glyphs of Warding into terrain to control movement.
source_quote: He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is referenced by Grygum as the one who committed to the trap on the bridge.
source_quote: Jorlan didn't hesitate, didn't slow — he came across that bridge like a man who had already decided the outcome

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is uninfected by the fungal corruption, sustained by hatred — which Asha Vandree identifies as its own kind of immunological theory. He is positioned on the bridge, inscribing a Glyph of Warding, and is perceived by Thorin as a predictable threat: a clear location to target. He is not part of the deception but a fixed variable in the tactical equation.
source_quote: Jorlan's side. He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself… Jorlan is not complicated. Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat because it tells you exactly where to aim.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan remained uninfected through hatred, which is its own kind of immunological theory, and maintained twenty feet of maintained distance.
source_quote: Only she and Jorlan remained uninfected — Asha through devotion, Jorlan through hatred, which is its own kind of immunological theory. Twenty feet of maintained distance.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator believes precision is not the opposite of force — it is force, directed.
source_quote: Precision is not the opposite of force. It is force, directed.

subject: Narrator
