source_quote: Soldiers. Now weapons. The difference between the two is sometimes just time and circumstance, and I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator finds the irony of being the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard almost invisible, even to themselves.
source_quote: The irony is almost invisible, even to me.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator prefers to file things away and not let stakes surface, but the stakes involving Asha keep surfacing.
source_quote: Asha was explicit enough about what's riding on this that I haven't been able to fully file it away the way I prefer to file things. It keeps surfacing.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator takes notes either way, whether Bahamut is watching or not.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching. I took notes either way.

subject: The Feared Mage of the Ember Vanguard
fact: The mage is the architect of the sculpted fireball, directing precise destructive force with calculated intent.
source_quote: I am the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin engaged Jorlan immediately after the glyph detonation, delivering a critical Dawnbringer strike and following up with a Sap to leave him disadvantaged — his aggression capitalized on the chaos.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan. The explosion was still ringing through the cavern when Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin exploits the chaos following the Glyph’s detonation to close on Jorlan, landing a critical Dawnbringer strike and a Sap to impose disadvantage; he notes the fragility of the spore servants and remains focused on the larger threat.
source_quote: Kaboom! I didn't expect it to work.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic tactician who borrows weapons, observes with cold precision, and files useful people and positions into a mental archive labeled *useful people*.
source_quote: I listened. I watched who spoke with certainty and who spoke with hedging.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Daz as the one who pressed the Sap after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: I was already closing on Jorlan. ... I pressed the Sap after it

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is unsinged after the fireball spell, as intended by the sculpted magic.
source_quote: I note that Thorin is unsinged.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the conditions under which the Sap succeeded: using momentum wrong to do something right.
source_quote: using the momentum wrong to do something right — shoving him off-balance

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the legendary action of the servant that landed a glancing blow for 5 damage.
source_quote: One of the servants wasn't finished with me. Legendary action, a swing that went so wide it almost circled back around to being impressive — natural 1, nothing — and then the follow-up connected for 5. Glancing. A reminder. Fair enough. I noted it.

subject: Valen
fact: Valen is referenced by Grygum as someone who could have been one of the repurposed guards.
source_quote: Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the fallen guards had been through quite a lot.
source_quote: Zalthir said, from his aerial vantage point, "Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt frustration wearing a physical costume after being poisoned.
source_quote: The poisoned condition settling over a person looks different depending on who they are. On Zalthir it looked like frustration wearing a physical costume.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir filed Ilvara’s scream of self-anger as a true indicator of damage inflicted, noting it as a psychological turning point.
source_quote: *She's angry at herself,* I noted, and filed it away, and watched.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a dragonborn who took the full brunt of the Heart Fungus’s spore cloud. He did not collapse dramatically, but exhibited a subtle wrongness in movement — a falter that signaled the poisoned condition settling over him. He disengaged and ascended ten feet, making a tactically sound but emotionally resigned decision. He declared himself out of actions and bonus actions, and chose to observe in dry confusion, his voice carrying the weight of a plan unraveling faster than expected.
source_quote: I'm out of actions and bonus actions, so I guess I'll just kind of look on and be confused.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a spellcaster who bypasses distance through teleportation, strikes without warning, and turns authority into target in the space of a decision.
source_quote: One moment I was reading the geometry... and the next I was already there, adjacent, inside the radius where a priestess stops being an authority and becomes a target.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is hovering above the battlefield, poisoned and frustrated, having disengaged after losing his tactical advantage over Ilvara; he is acutely aware of the repurposed guards and reflects silently on Valen's potential fate.
source_quote: Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by Grygum as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Zalthir might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is unsinged after the fireball spell, as intended by the sculpted magic.
source_quote: I note that Zalthir is unsinged.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, 'Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot,' from his aerial vantage point.
source_quote: Zalthir said, from his aerial vantage point, 'Those poor guards. They've been through quite a lot.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir teleported directly to Ilvara or grabbed her and moved her somewhere unpleasant, and filed teleportation as a weapon under *useful people*.
source_quote: Zalthir said he could teleport directly to Ilvara — or grab her and move her somewhere unpleasant. I stored that. Teleportation as a weapon. Thorin files that away in the part of his brain labeled *useful people.*

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is referenced as the source of the fungal colonization that repurposed the Velkynvelve guards.
source_quote: the fungal colonization of Zuggtmoy's influence made visible

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.
source_quote: The Big Heart Fungus was the primary weapon, would need sustained damage, would not die quickly or easily.

subject: Dancing Lights
fact: Dancing Lights were threaded down like a column of divine attention, absorbed into the speaker and blinking out.
source_quote: The Dancing Lights threading down like a column of divine attention, absorbed into the familiar, absorbed into me, blinking out.

subject: Dancing Lights
fact: The Dancing Lights were used by the narrator as an initial attempt to simulate divine presence; they were dismissed as a crude illusion by Asha, who recognized them as a common trick among charlatans.
source_quote: The Dancing Lights threading down like a column of divine attention, absorbed into the familiar, absorbed into me, blinking out.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is the blade Thorin used to deliver a critical hit to Jorlan after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: Dawnbringer came down — crit, the blade's light cutting into him hard and clean, 14 damage landing exactly where it needed to.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: A rare and costly resource cast directly onto the Big Heart Fungus to neutralize its anchoring power; its use signals a commitment to decisive action despite the risk of resource depletion.
source_quote: I committed the Dust of Suleiman and cast it directly onto the fungus.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman is a magical substance available to the party, capable of disintegrating organic matter. It is intended as a weapon against Ilvara, with the plan to force her into its area of effect. Its use is calculated and economical, meant to let the battlefield do the killing. It is not yet deployed but is a critical component of the tactical plan.
source_quote: I looked at the cavern floor. At the Dust of Suleiman area. At the rough arithmetic of: priestess plus that zone equals someone else's problem.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman was among the tactical options laid out by the party for battlefield control.
source_quote: Glyph of Warding. Dust of Suleiman. Phantasmal Killer. Fireball.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a non-replaceable resource committed to the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: This was not a small resource. I made the decision anyway

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a resource committed directly onto the Big Heart Fungus.
source_quote: I committed the Dust of Suleiman and cast it directly onto the fungus

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman was cast directly onto the Big Heart Fungus — a high-cost resource deployed despite risk, because the fungus had already demonstrated what it was willing to do.
source_quote: This was not a small resource. I made the decision anyway, because the creature had already demonstrated what it was willing to do to us.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman was positioned on the cavern floor as a zone of lethal environmental hazard.
source_quote: I looked at the cavern floor. At the Dust of Suleiman area.

subject: Fireball
fact: Fireball was among the options spread out on the Underdark equivalent of a table as a potential 4th-level spell deployment.
source_quote: Glyph of Warding. Dust of Suleiman. Phantasmal Killer. Fireball.

subject: Fireball
fact: The Fireball was cast at fourth level and dealt twelve damage to both Ilvara and the icon.
source_quote: Ilvara takes twelve. The icon takes twelve.

subject: Fireball
fact: The Fireball was cast at fourth level with eight dice, sculpted to avoid Zalthir and Thorin.
source_quote: Fireball. Cast at fourth level. Eight dice. ... I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them by the time it arrives and it will go around

subject: Fireball (Daz’s Sculpted)
fact: A fourth-level Fireball cast with Sculpt Spells to precisely target Ilvara and the Zuggtmoy icon while sparing allies; it deals 12 damage to each, altering the battlefield’s tactical calculus.
source_quote: Eight dice. I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them...

subject: Glyph
fact: The Glyph was a trap laid on the bridge as a bait — its activation relied on Jorlan’s predictable ego-driven advance, turning his confidence into his downfall.
source_quote: We'd laid it on the bridge like a welcome mat, and then the whole job was just: don't stand on it yourself, and wait.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: A Glyph of Warding inscribed into bridge stone creates an invisible, persistent trap — activated by hostile movement, serving as a silent guardian of the chokepoint.
source_quote: He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: A magically activated ward placed on the bridge by the party to exploit overconfidence; it detonates with force and light, dealing 21 damage in a sphere and destroying one spore servant while crippling Jorlan.
source_quote: The Glyph fired.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is a magical trap placed on the bridge with the explicit intent of exploiting chaotic battlefield conditions. It remains active and untriggered until Jorlan’s impulsive movement draws him into its range. It is not merely a spell — it is a tactical decision made in advance, a weapon of foresight. Its activation was inevitable once Jorlan was distracted. The glyph is a symbol of preparation, and its success proves that planning can outmaneuver raw power.
source_quote: We'd placed it with exactly this kind of chaos in mind

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding was inscribed into the stone of the bridge, with trigger: any hostile creature crossing, invisible once finished.
source_quote: Jorlan's side. He moved to the crossing and started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding was placed on the bridge by Grygum's idea and the group's execution.
source_quote: The Glyph was Grygum's idea, or at least Grygum's mouth. The placement was all of us.

subject: Glyph of Warding (on the bridge)
fact: A Glyph of Warding has been inscribed into the stone of the bridge by Jorlan, triggered by any hostile creature crossing. It is invisible once active, patient, and designed to serve as a perimeter defense. It is a tactical tool meant to delay or eliminate threats approaching from Jorlan’s side, and is understood by Thorin as a fixed variable in the battlefield geometry.
source_quote: Jorlan... started inscribing the Glyph of Warding into the stone itself... The trigger: any hostile creature crossing. Invisible once finished. Patient in the way only traps can be patient.

subject: glyph of warding value
fact: The Glyph of Warding was a tactical gamble — a trap laid to exploit ego overriding caution — and it succeeded, dealing 21 damage and killing one servant.
source_quote: The tactic had been a gamble — you call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness...

subject: Heart Fungus Spore Cloud
fact: The spore cloud is a physical manifestation of the Heart Fungus’s hostile will — a twenty-foot expanse of airborne poison that lingers, refuses to disperse, and selectively infects. It is not an accident of the environment; it is an intentional attack. It poisoned Zalthir, altered his movement, and forced a tactical retreat. The cloud is not a hazard — it is a weapon with memory, and its persistence marks the fungus as a sentient combatant.
source_quote: twenty feet of spore-thick poison, sitting in the middle of the battlefield as if it belonged there

subject: Ilvara's magical items
fact: Ilvara's magical items were offered as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.

subject: Light Crossbow
fact: A light crossbow, borrowed from Grygum, is the chosen ranged weapon — reliable, non-magical, and ideal for precise, non-committal engagement.
source_quote: Grygum had a light crossbow. I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism.

subject: Light Crossbow
fact: The light crossbow was borrowed from Grygum, checked for sloppiness by pulling the string, sighting down it, confirming the prior owner was not sloppy.
source_quote: I asked him for it. Simple transaction, no drama — he handed it over and I checked the mechanism the way you check anything borrowed before a fight: pull the string, sight down it, make sure the person who owned it before you wasn't sloppy.

subject: Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove
fact: The Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove is the original vector of corruption that enabled Ilvara’s transformation and the spread of the Big Heart Fungus. It is the catalyst, not the source, and remains a dangerous relic that must be contained or destroyed to halt the infection.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove
fact: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove is the mechanism of corruption — a dangerous object that must not be touched, known to induce madness or transformation.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Mushroom Artifact from Neverlight Grove
fact: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption, the trigger for the fungal transformation of Ilvara’s allies.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact from Neverlight Grove was the mechanism of corruption.

subject: Phantasmal Killer
fact: Phantasmal Killer was among the options spread out on the Underdark equivalent of a table as a potential 4th-level spell deployment.
source_quote: Glyph of Warding. Dust of Suleiman. Phantasmal Killer. Fireball.

subject: Sap
fact: The Sap is a maneuver Thorin used to shove Jorlan off-balance after the Glyph detonated.
source_quote: I pressed the Sap after it, using the momentum wrong to do something right — shoving him off-balance, leaving him on the back foot

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Spores
fact: Spores are the suspected vector of Ilvara’s corruption, transforming followers into mindless fungal entities; they are treated by Asha as a tangible, infectious agent rather than a metaphorical curse.
source_quote: have you two been infected by the spores… possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy?

subject: the fireball spell
fact: The fireball was shaped by intent to bypass specific targets and strike only designated ones, demonstrating mastery of spell sculpting.
source_quote: I carve them out. The fire will know the shape of them by the time it arrives and it will go around — not because fire cares, fire doesn't care about anything, but because I told it the shape of what it cannot touch.

subject: Zalthir's weapon
fact: Zalthir used a weapon that dealt sixteen damage on the first strike and fifteen on the second, totaling thirty-one.
source_quote: I drove the weapon in. Sixteen... The second strike... Fifteen more. Thirty-one total.

subject: Asha’s stakes
fact: The mission’s true stakes are tied to Asha — her words and warnings persistently surface in Daz’s calculations, making the Zuggtmoy icon more than a target — it’s a personal obligation.
source_quote: The stakes are not abstract. The stakes are Asha, and everything she told me...

subject: Asha's true loyalty
fact: Asha Vandree claims Lolth’s gratitude as sufficient — but her actions suggest deeper, unspoken motives, possibly independent of divine allegiance.
source_quote: I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that.

subject: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does
fact: The successful tactic combined psychological manipulation, precise timing, resource expenditure, and trusting a specialist’s instincts — this combination is now a documented pattern for future engagements.
source_quote: I noted the specific combination of factors that had produced that outcome: bait the ego, trust the glyph, commit the resource, let Daz do what Daz does.

subject: Big Heart Fungus
fact: The Big Heart Fungus remains standing and anchoring the far end of the battlefield — its continued existence is the root cause of the conflict and the reason Zalthir hovers above the fight.
source_quote: The fungus was still standing. Still anchoring the far end of the battlefield. Still the reason Zalthir was hovering above the fight instead of in it.

subject: contaminated magical items
fact: Ilvara's magical items may be contaminated — a potential trap or hidden threat that remains unverified and unaddressed.
source_quote: She offered Ilvara's magical items as additional payment, with the caveat that they might be contaminated.

subject: Ego vs. Tactical Awareness
fact: The success of the Glyph and Fireball depends on exploiting enemy overconfidence; this pattern is noted as a repeatable tactical lever, though its reliability remains uncertain.
source_quote: You call a man an idiot and invite him toward an explosive ward and you are making a bet on ego overriding tactical awareness...

subject: Ilvara's Corruption
fact: Ilvara’s descent into fungal worship and her transformation of allies into mindless spore-creatures represents a spreading contagion that threatens the balance of drow society; Asha Vandree believes it must be stopped before it infects more.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Ilvara's Corruption and the Spread of the Fungus
fact: The central unresolved thread is whether Ilvara’s corruption is reversible, and whether the Big Heart Fungus will continue to spread beyond the cavern. Asha fears the disease will spread, and the party must kill Ilvara before she can infect more of the Underdark. The fungal artifact and the spore cloud suggest this is not a localized event but an emerging plague.
source_quote: I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Jorlan's position
fact: Jorlan is a known threat with a fixed location — his presence on the bridge is both tactical and psychological, a target waiting to be aimed at.
source_quote: Jorlan is not complicated. Jorlan is a threat with a location, which is the best kind of threat because it tells you exactly where to aim.

subject: Narrator's Delusion
fact: The narrator has constructed a coherent delusion of divine possession and fungal influence to survive Asha’s scrutiny; while false, it has been accepted as plausible because it aligns with known patterns of corruption in the region, making it a viable cover.
source_quote: Perhaps my prayers have been answered through this… confused vessel… Perhaps there are some spores within me, but I… it feels… I feel it.

subject: remaining targets
fact: Ilvara and the icon are still standing after the spell, indicating the fight is not over despite the tactical shift.
source_quote: Ilvara is still standing. But twelve points is twelve points and the board looks different than it did thirty seconds ago.

subject: Screams Left Behind
fact: Ilvara’s scream — not at her attacker, but at herself — was left echoing in the cavern like a physical artifact. This thread suggests that trauma, when profound enough, becomes part of the environment. The scream is not just sound; it is the sound of an illusion shattering. It lingers as a warning, a marker of vulnerability, and a testament to the psychological cost of combat. The party is now fighting not just bodies, but echoes of broken wills.
source_quote: at herself.

subject: The Battlefield as an Enemy
fact: The cavern floor — through the Heart Fungus and Ilvara’s fungalized reanimation — has become an active, sentient antagonist. The party planned for drow commanders and spellcasters, but not for the environment itself to retaliate. This thread suggests the setting is not passive; it remembers, adapts, and claims those who die within it. The fungal growths are not just hazards — they are the bones of the past, repurposed. The party is not invading a dungeon — they are trespassing in a living graveyard that fights back.
source_quote: as if we were the interlopers in its home.

subject: The Fate of Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s nature remains ambiguous: is he a bound familiar, a sentient fungal offshoot, or an independent entity masquerading as a pet? His presence defies categorization, and his role in the mission is unspoken. He may be a liability, a weapon, or a harbinger — his true origin is a thread left deliberately unresolved.
source_quote: Glabbagool attempted to pass for a rock... He looked at me. Or at least, several of his eyes moved in my general direction.

subject: The Floor as Enemy
fact: The party realizes the battlefield itself — the cavern floor and its fungal growth — is an active, sentient threat, not just terrain; this shifts their tactical paradigm from fighting enemies to fighting the environment.
source_quote: You plan for the drow commander. You don't always plan for the floor itself to become an enemy.

subject: the goal all along
fact: The true objective — eyeing the prize — has never shifted, even as tactics, alliances, and weapons changed hands.
source_quote: *The goal the whole time*, I thought. *Eyeing the prize.*

subject: The Nature of Daz's Connection to Lolth
fact: Daz claims to feel Lolth’s gratitude — but whether he truly does, or is simply performing a delusion that has become real through belief, is unknown. His steadiness suggests internal conviction. Is he a fraud who became a prophet? Or a prophet who was mistaken for a fraud? This thread underlies the entire negotiation and may determine the party’s spiritual fate.
source_quote: I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that... It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Things Not to Dwell On Mid-Combat
fact: The party recognizes the emotional weight of repurposed enemies and fallen allies as dangerous distractions; these thoughts are filed away as 'not to dwell on' to preserve combat effectiveness.
source_quote: I filed that thought away under *things not to dwell on mid-combat*.

subject: Valen
fact: Valen could have been one of the repurposed soldiers, and somewhere between then and now, he had lost the thread entirely.
source_quote: Then he reflected on Valen. Not out loud, really — it was more in the quality of the silence that followed. I felt the thought land in the room anyway. Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized. These bodies on the cavern floor had once been exactly what Valen was, and somewhere between then and now, they had lost the thread entirely.

subject: Valen’s Fate
fact: Valen’s potential transformation into one of the fungalized guards was silently reflected upon by Zalthir. The thought hung in the air — that Valen, once a living drow soldier, could have become what now rises from the floor. This thread connects identity, corruption, and the thin line between soldier and weapon. It is not spoken aloud, but its emotional weight lingers, suggesting a deeper narrative about loss, control, and what happens when people are repurposed by forces beyond their will.
source_quote: Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.

subject: Valen’s Fate
fact: Zalthir silently reflects on Valen — who was once like the repurposed guards — and the thin line between identity and corruption; this unresolved emotional thread haunts the party’s understanding of the enemy’s humanity.
source_quote: Valen, who had been one of them. Who could have been one of them, differently categorized.
